transcript: This is bed four, Mr Alvarez, sixty-eight, came in with chest pain at six this morning. He has a history of hypertension and is allergic to penicillin. His obs are stable, blood pressure one thirty over eighty, sats ninety-seven on air. Please repeat the ECG in an hour and chase the troponin.

Bed twelve is Mrs Okafor, admitted overnight with shortness of breath. Known COPD, usually takes salbutamol at home. Sats are eighty-eight on room air, she looks tired but is talking in full sentences. Needs hourly obs and escalate if sats drop below eighty-five.

This is the gentleman in bay two, came in after a fall at home. Background of atrial fibrillation, on apixaban. His GCS is fifteen, no obvious head injury, pain score six in the left hip. Please chase the hip x-ray and keep him nil by mouth.

Bed seven, young woman presenting with abdominal pain since yesterday. No significant past medical history, not on any regular medication. Temperature is thirty-eight two, heart rate one hundred and ten, she appears uncomfortable. Recommend repeat bloods in four hours and review by the surgical team.

This is bed nine, elderly gentleman brought in confused. History of dementia and a previous stroke. Obs are within normal limits, afebrile, but he is disoriented to time and place. Please keep an eye on him, he has been trying to mobilise unaided.

Bed one, patient is post-operative day two following appendicectomy. Previously fit and well, no allergies. Wound looks clean, pain score two, tolerating diet. Continue current analgesia and the surgical team will review in the morning.
